## 614b8ee6-6a63-4ee9-b948-d4fb9064d6be / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The selected experiment-9 checkpoint remains competent but variable: it achieved 193/200, 176/200, and 182/200 on the panels at episode seeds 6600, 6800, and 7000. On the latest panel, failures clustered in the inner radial band and near the angular edges, while successful episodes commonly reached and held the target. Complete success still couples departure from the singular reset, approach, tolerance entry, settling, and uninterrupted holding rather than exposing one isolated failure stage.

**Lessons and limits:** In the latest 200-episode panel, 18 failures all failed to record tolerance entry; 16 had targets between 6 and 11 cm, and 14 of those were in the roughly -175 to -125 degree region while the other two were near the positive angular edge. One separate failure came within 1.4 cm without entering. Earlier broad-radius and angle-focused training changes also regressed on their tested trajectories, and training proxies have repeatedly failed to predict complete behavior. These observations weaken simple coverage explanations without identifying whether target geometry, posture selection, braking, local regulation, or their interaction is responsible. The selected lineage remains below the 98% objective, and the panel results are development evidence rather than final validation.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved how the reset singularity, target radius and angle, inverse-kinematic branch, and direct-torque trajectory combine in the residual failures. It is also unresolved whether the apparent concentration near inner angular-edge targets persists across further disjoint episodes and whether changes that improve those episodes preserve entry, settling, and sustained holding elsewhere.
